analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers Louisiana Purchase of 1803 with land size cost and authorization limit, Jefferson constitutional doubts, 19th century expansion series, slavery related sectional compromises including Compromise of 1850, Native displacement, and treaty structure with two conventions

overview.headline: Louisiana Purchase doubled nation size and deepened slavery and Native conflicts

keyPoints.point: The United States purchased land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million and doubled its size expanding westward
keyPoints.quote: the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million

keyPoints.point: Negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe were authorized to pay up to $10 million for New Orleans and the Floridas before accepting larger offer
keyPoints.quote: negotiators Robert Livingston and James Monroe were authorized to pay France up to $10 million solely for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas

keyPoints.point: President Jefferson as strict interpreter wondered if Government was authorized to acquire new territory despite expansion desire
keyPoints.quote: was generally a strict interpreter of the Constitution who wondered if the U.S. Government

keyPoints.point: Expansions exposed sectional weaknesses between North and South related to slavery requiring fragile compromises
keyPoints.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery

keyPoints.point: Land ceded was populated with thousands of American Indians across dozens of tribes later forcibly moved to reservations
keyPoints.quote: The land ceded in this agreement (and later expansions) was populated with thousands of American Indians across dozens of tribes.

keyTerms.gloss: transfer of land where territory is ceded as part of expansion series
keyTerms.quote: The Louisiana Purchase was the first major cession of land in a long series of expansions that span the 19th century.

keyTerms.gloss: sectional divisions between North and South related to slavery that made compromises fragile
keyTerms.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery

keyTerms.gloss: fragile compromise to maintain balance between free states and slave states
keyTerms.quote: notably the Missouri Compromise and the Compromise of 1850

keyTerms.gloss: people whose potential impact was ignored when land was ceded
keyTerms.quote: In addition, the Louisiana Purchase ignored the potential impact on Native Americans.

keyTerms.gloss: Treaty that ceded Louisiana territory and included two financial conventions
keyTerms.quote: The Louisiana Purchase Agreement is made up of the Treaty of Cession and the two conventions regarding the financial aspects of the transaction.
